title: A relative repository path in a profile resolves against the shell's directory, not the profile's
foundBy: session agent, while choosing a repository path for the example campaign

evidence.verified: TestARelativeTreeResolvesBesideTheProfile and TestInitWritesTheTreesItWasGivenAsAbsolutePaths pass under `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1`. The first plans from another directory and finds `app`, `./specs` and `../shared` resolved beside the profile, with nothing written where the shell stood. Removing the resolver fails it. The second runs `init --dir sub/demo --repo ./app` and finds the path written relative to the shell. Removing the step that writes it absolute fails it. The full gate, `make check`, passes.

resolution: Decoding a profile now resolves each relative repository and snapshot path against the profile's directory, where its mission and briefs are found. `--repo` and `--snapshot` on the command line stay relative to the shell. `init` writes them into the profile as absolute paths, so a scaffold still names what was typed wherever `--dir` puts it. The manual's Configuration section and SPEC.md's profile table state the rule.
details:
A profile finds its mission and briefs beside itself, wherever it is read from. A repository declared as `path: ./app` resolves through `expandPath` in `internal/cli/profile.go`, which takes it relative to the current directory instead. The same profile therefore names a different repository depending on where the operator stands.

The cost lands at create. When the path does not exist, plan pins a first commit and create makes the repository. A relative path therefore makes a new repository in whatever directory the shell was in. A profile copied with its briefs into another directory keeps its briefs and loses its repository.

To reproduce, write a profile whose members declare `path: ./app`, and run `cs-campaign plan <name> --profile <dir>/profile.yaml --dry-run` from a different directory. Each `repos[].path` in the plan names `./app` under the shell's directory, not under `<dir>`.

Neither the manual nor SPEC.md says which base a relative path takes. Resolving it beside the profile, as the briefs are, would make a profile directory self-contained.
